detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

The big man is sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set Monday, but he should be good to go for Wednesday's showdown in Denver. Mitchell Robinson is the most likely choice to replace Queta in the starting lineup, while Luka Garza should see a sizable chunk of the center minutes.
Awaka is missing a fifth straight contest due to a back problem. The rookie big man can be considered week-to-week going forward.

The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Tyson is expected to miss a second consecutive contest with a right ankle injury. If Peyton Watson (back), who is listed as questionable, and Tyson are both ruled out, Meleek Thomas, Tyrese Proctor and Mario Hezonja could all see increased burn.

Merrill has missed the past six games due to a right elbow issue, but this is the first time he's received the questionable tag since going down, which indicates progress. If he is cleared to return, Meleek Thomas' minutes could dip.
Lawal is on track to sit out Wednesday's game. However, he's not a consistent part of the rotation, so his absence from the active roster won't impact fantasy leagues.
The 40-year-old big man could receive some load management for the first half of this back-to-back set. Charles Bassey could be a decent streaming option in fantasy leagues if Horford sits out.

Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.
Phillips will shake off his questionable tag for Wednesday's regular-season opener. However, the two-way player isn't likely to be part of the Rockets' rotation.

McConnell's minutes have been steadily ramping up since he made his regular-season debut on Nov. 7, and he had his best game yet in Sunday's 131-124 loss to the 76ers, finishing with 12 points, five rebounds, five assists and one steal in 19 minutes off the bench. As long as Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) is sidelined, McConnell should be able to earn enough minutes to provide some low-end value in fantasy leagues with his output in assists and steals.

Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

This will be Stewart's second straight game on the sidelines, which should lead to more minutes for Taylor Hendricks and Quinten Post. Stewart's next chance to play will come Thursday against the Warriors.

This will be Jerome's third straight game on the inactive list due to the hip injury, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Thursday's meeting with the Warriors. Cam Spencer should continue to start in his absence and Javon Small will have the chance for some extended minutes. Cedric Coward should continue to see some increased playmaking responsibilities with Jerome sidelined.
Gardner is battling a hamstring injury ahead of Wednesday's action. With Pelle Larsson (illness) available, Gardner's short-term fantasy appeal appears to be expiring.
Jovic is trending in the right direction following a one-game absence due to an illness. However, his return wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

The star big man was pulled as a precaution Monday against Houston due to a hip issue, and he's not expected to miss more time. After scoring in double figures in nine consecutive appearances prior to Monday's abbreviated outing, Adebayo will be aiming to start a new double-digit points streak Wednesday.

Kuminga sustained a bruised shoulder during Monday's meeting with the Trail Blazers, and he's sitting out the second part of this back-to-back set. Terrence Shannon appears to be the most likely candidate to replace Kuminga in the starting lineup, while Trey Lyles and Bones Hyland will both have a chance to claim a larger role.

This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.
Sorber is still recovering from knee surgery and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Thunder offer an update on his status.

This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

After playing 30 minutes during Monday's loss to Minnesota, the star point forward is in danger of missing the second half of this back-to-back set. Damian Lillard would do the heavy lifting offensively if Avdija sits out Tuesday, while either Jrue Holiday or Scoot Henderson would likely enter the starting lineup.

Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.
LaVine was ruled out shortly before tipoff after falling ill. Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk should be in line for additional opportunities Sunday with LaVine sidelined.
McCullar quickly finds a new home after being waived by the Knicks in late October. The forward is expected to play a prominent role for Toronto's G League affiliate.

Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.
